common_name: Anticipation Camellia (Rosy Crimson Peony-Form Jury Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or spring into humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; the narrow, upright habit suits a tight bed or courtyard corner better than a sprawling border.

directions: Bred by Les Jury in New Zealand, Anticipation carries large, paeony-form, rosy crimson flowers roughly five inches across on a narrow, upright plant, one of the most richly colored of the Jury williamsii hybrids. The heavy blooms can bow thin new shoots in open wind, so give young plants a sheltered spot for their first few winters. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after the spring flush fades, and prune only to shape right after bloom so next year's buds are not removed.

common_name: Grand Jury Camellia (Apricot-Pink Peony-Form Jury Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or spring into moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; give it room to spread since the habit is broader than many compact williamsii cultivars.

directions: A Les Jury introduction from New Zealand dating to 1964, Grand Jury bears large, paeony-form flowers in a soft apricot-pink, about five inches across, among the warmer-toned blooms in the williamsii group. Its vigorous, spreading growth works well as a specimen or informal screen along a shaded path. Keep the root zone mulched and evenly moist through summer heat to support strong bud set, and avoid heavy pruning since flower buds form on the current season's wood.

common_name: Elegant Beauty Camellia (Anemone-Centered Jury Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or spring into humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this 1962 Les Jury introduction has a lanky habit that benefits from light structural pruning when young.

directions: Bred by Les Jury in New Zealand in 1962, Elegant Beauty is grown chiefly for its anemone-centered flowers, similar in form to the japonica cultivar 'Elegans', over a winter-into-spring season. Its naturally lanky, somewhat open habit benefits from light shaping in the first few years to build a fuller frame. Mulch well and water deeply during dry spells in the first two seasons to establish a strong root system, and prune only to shape right after bloom since next year's buds set soon afterward.

common_name: J.C. Williams Camellia (Single Light Pink Original Caerhays Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or spring into moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade; this is the original Caerhays williamsii cross, first exhibited in 1942 and named for J.C. Williams who first raised the hybrid group in Cornwall.

directions: J.C. Williams is the namesake cultivar of the entire Camellia x williamsii hybrid group, raised at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall from a cross between C. japonica and C. saluenensis and first exhibited in 1942. Its single, light dog-rose pink flowers with deeper shadings open wide and are of notably good substance, blooming over a long winter-into-spring season on a vigorous, upright shrub. Because it is one of the hardier and more historically significant williamsii cultivars, it suits collectors' gardens and woodland-edge plantings alike; feed lightly after bloom and prune only to shape, since next year's buds set on the current season's growth.

common_name: November Pink Camellia (Early-Blooming Light Crimson Caerhays Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall into moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade with protection from hard freezes, since this cultivar opens its first flowers earlier than most camellias.

directions: Raised at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, November Pink lives up to its name by opening single, light crimson flowers about three and a half inches wide as early as late autumn, continuing into spring and well ahead of most other camellias. Site it away from the coldest exposure so the earliest buds are not damaged by a hard frost before they open. Keep roots mulched and evenly moist through summer to support strong early bud set, and prune only immediately after flowering to avoid removing next season's buds.

common_name: George Blandford Camellia (Deep Clear Pink Peony-Form Caerhays Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or spring into humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, as with other Caerhays-raised williamsii hybrids; a cross with C. japonica 'Lady Clare' as one parent.

directions: Raised at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall from a cross involving the japonica cultivar 'Lady Clare', George Blandford bears paeony-form flowers in a deep, clear pink on a sturdy, rounded shrub, opening rather early in the camellia season. It flowers over a long winter-into-spring window and holds its shape well with minimal pruning, making it a dependable choice for a mixed shrub border or specimen planting. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer after the main bloom period and keep the shallow root zone mulched through summer heat.

common_name: Water Lily Camellia (Lavender-Pink Formal Double High-Centered Williamsii Hybrid)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or spring into moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; this 1967 New Zealand introduction has formal double flowers that hold their shape best out of hard rain and wind.

directions: Introduced from New Zealand in 1967, Water Lily is one of the best-known williamsii hybrids, bearing formal double flowers with a distinctive high center, light pink shaded with lavender-pink. Its tidy, symmetrical bloom form makes it a favorite for cutting as well as garden display, flowering over a long winter-into-spring season. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom and prune only to shape immediately afterward, since next year's flower buds set on the current season's growth.

common_name: Autumn Spirit Camellia (Cold-Hardy Pink Peony-Form Oleifera-Sasanqua Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial sun; Autumn Spirit was introduced by Camellia Forest Nursery in 2008, crossing the Lu Shan strain of cold-hardy Camellia oleifera with C. sasanqua for improved winter hardiness.

directions: Autumn Spirit was introduced by Camellia Forest Nursery in 2008 from a cross of the cold-hardy Lu Shan strain of Camellia oleifera with Camellia sasanqua, aiming to combine fall bloom with better winter survival than sasanqua alone offers. It bears peony-form pink flowers two and a half to three inches across in early fall, on a dense, rounded evergreen shrub useful as a screen or specimen at the colder edge of camellia range. Feed lightly with an acid-forming fertilizer after bloom, keep the root zone mulched, and prune only to shape immediately after flowering finishes.
